what_it_does: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) is a mathematical technique that lets a computer run AI calculations directly on encrypted data — the server never sees the raw inputs, which is ideal for private medical or financial queries. The catch is that FHE operations are roughly 10,000 times slower than ordinary arithmetic, making it impractical for large AI models. Previous specialized chips to accelerate FHE used single very large designs that were expensive and did not scale to bigger models like BERT (a large language-understanding AI). Cinnamon is a framework that instead uses multiple smaller chips (chiplets) working together, connected by a network that the researchers designed to minimize how much data must be sent between chips. A compiler automatically finds and schedules parallelism in the FHE computation, and new algorithms reduce the communication overhead between chiplets, together bringing FHE-accelerated AI inference closer to practical deployment.
